title: Remove, Improve, Zoom
opening: Making a recurring explanation faster may leave the repeated work intact. An adequate existing explanation might remove that burden. Human help can still be necessary where an independent attempt reveals a real gap, so removing every conversation would lose part of the purpose.

labels.comparisonIntro: Compare what changes when a repeated introductory call is removed, when the remaining help improves, and when participation grows. The necessary learning and the experience people value still matter.
labels.rhythmTitle: Preserve the function when the arrangement changes
labels.rhythmText: A faster process that produces the wrong result has lost something necessary. Restore or replace that function. A rare, complex case may be best served by a faster manual conversation; removal is a question to investigate, not a result every case has to reach.
labels.practiceIntro: Describe its purpose and what would happen if it disappeared. Then compare what can be removed, what needs improvement and what a change in scale or attention reveals.

labels.sourceQuote:
Remove, Improve, Zoom
This is the purpose of Remove, Improve, Zoom. Question whether the requirement or
activity needs to exist. Remove what has no necessary job. Improve what remains.
Then change speed, scale or level of attention to reveal the next useful issue. New
evidence can send you back through the sequence.
labels.sampleLoaded: Example loaded. Replace it with your own observations when useful.
labels.removeText: Ask what the introductory call does. An existing explanation might supply the routine introduction. Keep or replace any necessary function before removing the call; deleting useful practice or valued conversation is not automatically an improvement.
labels.improveText: Improve the work that remains. Human help might focus on the difficulty an independent attempt actually exposed. Check whether the learner can use the method, rather than measuring only how quickly the explanation was delivered.
labels.zoomText: Change speed, scale or the level you examine. More participants may reveal limits in access, review or support. A closer look at one attempt may expose a confusing instruction. Use what that change reveals to revisit what should be removed or improved.

fields.label: The activity, its purpose and the participation that matters
What can disappear, and how is any necessary function preserved?
What improvement does the remaining work need?
What does a change in speed, scale or attention reveal?
What new evidence sends you through the three moves again?

example.purpose: In this example, a repeated call introduces the same method and sometimes supplies help with a real learner difficulty.
example.remove: Reuse an adequate existing introduction. Keep suitable help where the learner’s own attempt reveals a gap.
example.improve: Focus the remaining help on the observed difficulty and check whether the person can use the method afterward.
example.zoom: At greater participation, inspect review capacity, access and resources. At a closer scale, inspect a representative attempt.
example.return: If the replacement leaves people confused or transfers hidden work to them, revisit the removal and preserve the missing function.
